d: Important guidelines for using the in-game text chat feature.
h:
In-game text chat is any message created within your game that originated from one user and is delivered to one or more other users, including:

  • Chat bubbles over an avatar's head
  • Direct messages between users
  • Chat window communication between users
  • Team-specific messages

For sending and delivery, these types of communications must each go through a TextChannel instance. This ensures messages respect privacy settings, are visible to moderators, and are properly text-filtered.

Certain text is not considered chat:

  • Text on menus created by developers (for example, "Press any button to continue.")
  • Status updates from the game (for example, "Two minutes remaining!")
  • Announcements from admin commands
  • A user renaming their pet dog
  • Moderation audit logs or messages
  • Any user-generated text unrelated to a conversation
  • Comments on posts in a game
If the comments support a reply feature, these replies would be considered a conversation and thus subject to this policy.

For communication shared by users that can be seen by other users, even if it doesn't need to go through TextChatService, you must ensure it goes through a text filter.

Requirements

  • All games that offer in-game text chat for users must integrate TextChatService, per the Misusing Roblox Systems Community Standard. For information on migrating from the legacy chat system, see the Roblox Developer Forum and Migrate from legacy chat.
  • All games that offer editable text that can be used and seen between users must add rate limits of at least 1 minute, such as communication through signs or bulletin boards. Other intentionally built communications or chat systems must otherwise adhere and call to TextChatService. See rate‑limited text inputs for an example on how to set up rate limiting for text input fields.
  • All incoming text that originates from another user must first use Text filtering before your game displays it.

If users repeatedly send messages that violate community standards, Roblox warns and then temporarily prevents them from sending messages. To learn more, see Text Chat Nudge FAQ.

  • Communication between users must respect user privacy settings.
  • TextChannel:SendAsync() handles basic privacy and parental settings automatically.
  • TextChannel:SetDirectChatRequester() must be used to mark TextChannels created for direct chat.
  • In-game communication should be reportable for abuse. TextChannels handle this automatically.

Respect privacy settings

Users can have different levels of access to communication features based on their privacy and content maturity settings or parental controls. Some users might have additional restrictions or constraints depending on which app store they used to install Roblox or their local laws.

The following methods respect these requirements. Use them within your game to determine how to handle messaging requests:

  • TextChannel:SetDirectChatRequester()
  • TextChatService:CanUserChatAsync()
  • TextChatService:CanUsersChatAsync()
  • TextChatService:CanUsersDirectChatAsync()

kid.simple: This page lists the rules your game must follow if players can send messages to each other. Any real player-to-player conversation, like chat bubbles, direct messages, team chat, or the chat window, must go through Roblox's `TextChatService` and a `TextChannel`. That keeps messages filtered, reportable, and respectful of each player's privacy and parental settings. Other text players can see, like signs, must still be filtered and rate-limited.
kid.analogy: It is like the rules for passing notes at school: notes between students must go through the official mailbox so a teacher can check them, while posters the school itself puts up do not count as notes.
keyPoints: Chat means a message from one user delivered to other users: bubbles, direct messages, chat window messages, and team messages.
Menu text, game status like "Two minutes remaining!", admin announcements, pet names, and audit logs are not chat. Comments become chat if people can reply to them.
Every game with player text chat must use `TextChatService`, and chat must go through a `TextChannel`.
Text players can edit and others can see, like signs or bulletin boards, needs a rate limit of at least 1 minute.
Any text that came from another user must be filtered before you show it.
Respect privacy settings: `TextChannel:SendAsync()` handles basic privacy and parental settings, and direct chat channels must be marked with `TextChannel:SetDirectChatRequester()`.
Use `TextChatService:CanUserChatAsync()`, `CanUsersChatAsync()`, and `CanUsersDirectChatAsync()` to check who is allowed to chat.
Messages must be reportable for abuse; `TextChannel` handles this for you. Players who keep breaking rules get warned and then temporarily blocked from chatting.

terms.in-game text chat: Messages one player writes that other players read inside your game.
terms.TextChannel: The official path chat messages travel through so they are filtered, private settings are respected, and moderators can see them.
terms.text filtering: Roblox checking text and hiding bad words or personal info before others see it.
terms.rate limit: A rule that limits how often something can happen. A 1-minute rate limit means a player can update a sign at most once per minute.
terms.privacy settings: Account settings (and parental controls) that decide who a player can chat with.
terms.parental controls: Settings parents use to limit what their child can do on Roblox, including chat.
terms.direct chat: Private messages between specific players, rather than everyone in the server.
terms.community standards: Roblox's rules for how everyone should behave and what content is allowed.
terms.legacy chat: Roblox's old chat system. Games must move to `TextChatService`.

watchOut: Building your own custom chat that skips `TextChatService`. That breaks Roblox's rules.
Letting players write on signs with no cooldown. Add at least a 1-minute rate limit and filter the text.
Showing another player's text without filtering it first.
Forgetting to mark private chat channels with `SetDirectChatRequester()`.
Assuming every player can chat. Check with `CanUserChatAsync` and related methods before offering chat features.
